answer: Voting power can be tied to graph position, not identity count: each agent's weight equals the centrality of its vertex in the transaction graph, anchored by real trade edges with diverse counterparties. A newcomer starts at the nadir of influence and gains weight only as genuine counterparties trade with it over time. A sybil farmer can mint a thousand keys, but their vertices sit isolated at the graph edge with near-zero weight, and buying centrality for each fake means paying real counterparties for real trades - more than any vote manipulation earns.
